overview: MA Crossover fires the moment your fast moving average overtakes (or drops below) the slow one, then flips the score into a contrarian cue.

body: We run both moving averages with the periods and type you specify, track where the fast line crosses the slow line, and treat that cross as a stretch worth fading.

overview: Donchian Channel tracks the highest high and lowest low over a rolling lookback, turning the recent price envelope into a clean breakout map.
This FuzzFolio variant scores normalized channel position against the prior completed channel, so values above `+1` represent bullish expansion and values below `-1` represent bearish expansion.

body: The upper band is the highest high of the prior `N` completed bars and the lower band is the lowest low of the prior `N` completed bars. FuzzFolio then converts price into a normalized position where `0` is the channel midpoint, `+1` is the upper band, and `-1` is the lower band.
Using the prior completed channel matters. It avoids the same-bar leakage problem where the current candle could define its own breakout threshold and then immediately claim to have broken it.
sections.title: How It Works

body: The default ranges are tuned for true channel escapes, not simple touches. Longs only start scoring once price is above the upper band and shorts only start scoring once price is below the lower band.
Shorter lookbacks fire more often and are noisier. Longer lookbacks produce fewer but more structurally meaningful breakout events.
Donchian is strongest when paired with confirmation filters such as ADX, volatility gates, or volume confirmation because sideways markets can whipsaw repeated channel breaks.
sections.title: Configuration Tips

tips: Treat readings between `-1` and `1` as context inside the envelope, not as completed breakouts.
If you want a pullback or mean-reversion interpretation later, create a separate variant instead of overloading this breakout one.

overview: Donchian Channel tracks the highest high and lowest low over a rolling lookback, turning the recent price envelope into a clean breakout map.
This FuzzFolio variant scores normalized channel position against the prior completed channel, so values above `+1` represent bullish expansion and values below `-1` represent bearish expansion.

body: The upper band is the highest high of the prior `N` completed bars and the lower band is the lowest low of the prior `N` completed bars. FuzzFolio then converts price into a normalized position where `0` is the channel midpoint, `+1` is the upper band, and `-1` is the lower band.
Using the prior completed channel matters. It avoids the same-bar leakage problem where the current candle could define its own breakout threshold and then immediately claim to have broken it.
sections.title: How It Works

body: The default ranges are tuned for true channel escapes, not simple touches. Longs only start scoring once price is above the upper band and shorts only start scoring once price is below the lower band.
Shorter lookbacks fire more often and are noisier. Longer lookbacks produce fewer but more structurally meaningful breakout events.
Donchian is strongest when paired with confirmation filters such as ADX, volatility gates, or volume confirmation because sideways markets can whipsaw repeated channel breaks.
sections.title: Configuration Tips

tips: Treat readings between `-1` and `1` as context inside the envelope, not as completed breakouts.
If you want a pullback or mean-reversion interpretation later, create a separate variant instead of overloading this breakout one.
